title: Italian-Style Pasta Salad with Mozzarella, Olives and Peppers
summary: A fresh Italian-style pasta salad loaded with juicy cherry tomatoes, mini mozzarella, olives and peppers, all tossed in a tangy herb dressing. It's an easy make-ahead side that tastes even better after a day in the fridge.
equipment: whisk or jam jar with a lid

ingredients.item: fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (1%)
ingredients.note: about 6¾ tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
red pepper, seeded and cut into thin strips

steps.title: Cook the Pasta
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to a rolling boil in the large pot and stir in the salt, then add the pasta and cook it for 1 minute longer than the packet suggests. Cold pasta firms up as it cools, so starting it fully tender rather than al dente keeps the texture pleasant once chilled. Drain in the colander, rinse briefly under cold water to stop the cooking, shake off as much water as you can, and spread it out on the baking tray to cool.

steps.title: Whisk the Dressing
steps.text: While the pasta cooks, whisk the vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, chilli flakes, salt and pepper together in a small bowl or jar. Once combined, whisk in the olive oil until the dressing looks slightly thickened and even. Building the acid and seasoning first helps them dissolve properly before the oil goes in, so the dressing doesn't end up tasting flat.

steps.title: Dress the Warm Pasta
steps.text: Tip the still-slightly-warm pasta into the large bowl and toss with two-thirds of the dressing, then leave it for 10 minutes, tossing once more partway through. Warm pasta is more porous and soaks up dressing rather than simply being coated in it, so this step is what gives the salad real flavour rather than a slick surface.

steps.title: Add the Salad Ingredients
steps.text: With the dressing made, scatter in the cherry tomatoes, red pepper strips, mozzarella balls, olives and red onion, then pour over the remaining dressing and toss everything together gently. Look for an even coating with no dry patches of pasta. Keeping the mozzarella balls whole rather than tearing them means each bite still gets a soft, milky contrast to the tangy dressing.

steps.title: Fold in the Basil
steps.text: Just before serving, fold the torn basil through the salad so the leaves stay bright and glossy rather than wilting in the dressing. Add it at the last minute, since basil bruises and turns a dull green quickly once it meets acid and salt.

steps.title: Check the Seasoning
steps.text: Give the salad a final taste once it has chilled, as cold food naturally tastes less seasoned than food at room temperature. Add a little extra salt or a squeeze of lemon if it needs brightening up. This last check is worth doing every time, since the balance that felt right earlier can fade in the fridge.

tips: Common mistake: dressing the pasta once it's completely cold — toss it in while still slightly warm so it actually absorbs the dressing instead of just sitting in it.
Shake the pasta really dry after rinsing; leftover water dilutes the dressing and leaves the salad watery.
Add the basil right before serving rather than mixing it in early, or it will wilt and turn dark.
Taste again after chilling and adjust salt or lemon — cold salads often need a touch more seasoning than warm ones.
Use mini mozzarella balls rather than larger ones, drained well, so every forkful gets some.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Stir through a splash of extra olive oil and a few fresh basil leaves before serving to freshen it up, as the pasta will have soaked up some of the dressing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
